issue_snapshot.title: non-deterministic output from compile templates when using tuple unpacking
issue_snapshot.body:
<!--
This issue tracker is a tool to address bugs in Jinja itself. Please use
GitHub Discussions or the Pallets Discord for questions about your own code.

Replace this comment with a clear outline of what the bug is.
-->
Ideally compile_templates will have deterministic output so we can use git diff etc

See also https://github.com/pallets/jinja/issues/1453 and https://github.com/pallets/jinja/issues/1452

Found another case where this occurs, e.g. I'm randomly getting these changes or their inverse:

```diff
-    context.vars.update({'triage_reports': l_0_triage_reports, 'open_group_index': l_0_open_group_index})
-    context.exported_vars.update(('triage_reports', 'open_group_index'))
+    context.vars.update({'open_group_index': l_0_open_group_index, 'triage_reports': l_0_triage_reports})
+    context.exported_vars.update(('open_group_index', 'triage_reports'))
```
or:
```diff
-                _loop_vars.update({'row_spans': l_2_row_spans, 'row': l_2_row})
+                _loop_vars.update({'row': l_2_row, 'row_spans': l_2_row_spans})
```
<!--
Describe how to replicate the bug.

Include a minimal reproducible example that demonstrates the bug.
Include the full traceback if there was an exception.
-->
I can see that both of the cases above are a result of using tuple unpacking to set multiple new context vars in a single `set` call
e.g.
```jinja
{% set triage_reports, open_group_index = get_nav_list_items(TRIAGE_REPORTS_NAV, url_name, url_func=url) %}
```
```jinja
{% set row, row_spans = row %}
```

<!--
Describe the expected behavior that should have happened but didn't.
-->
The output from compiling the templates should be stable if the underlying template hasn't changed, rather than varying randomly each time you run it.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.11.5
- Jinja version: 3.1.4

issue_snapshot.body:

- [x] I agree to follow the [aio-libs Code of Conduct][CoC]

any hesitation exists.)*

[vulnerability report form]: ../security/advisories/new

- [ ] I am willing to submit a pull request with reporoducers as xfailing test cases or even entire fix. *(Assign this issue to me.)*

### Describe the bug

Calling `with_suffix` always re-encode the entire name. That's because `with_suffix` calls `with_name` under the hood, which always auto encodes

from the method's description: 

> suffix is encoded if needed

https://github.com/aio-libs/yarl/blob/07c1b4fd53728bf26937e14e6f988c5766d0ac69/yarl/_url.py#L1350-L1354

### To Reproduce

```python
from yarl import URL
url = URL("https://domain.com/video file.mp4")
print (url) # https://domain.com/video%20file.mp4
print (url.with_suffix(".avi")) # https://domain.com/video%2520file.avi
```

### Expected behavior



Only the suffix should be encoded (if needed) instead of the entire name. 

Therefore, the expected result would be `https://domain.com/video%20file.avi` instead of `https://domain.com/video%2520file.avi`




### Logs/tracebacks

```python-traceback
NA
```

### Python Version

```console
$ python --version
Python 3.13.2
```

### multidict Version

```console
$ python -m pip show multidict
Version: 6.1.0
```

### propcache Version

```console
$ python -m pip show propcache
Version: 0.2.1
```

### yarl Version

```console
$ python -m pip show yarl
Version: 1.18.3
```

### OS

Windows 10

### Additional context

_No response_

issue_snapshot.title: S3 client download_fileobj became incompatible with GzipFile from stdlib
issue_snapshot.body:
### Describe the bug

`with gzip.open(path, 'file.gz', mode='wb+'): as gzip_file:`
`                   s3_client.download_fileobj(bucket, key, gzip_file,`
`                                           Config=TransferConfig(use_threads=False))`

The code above used to work prior to @ #4503 , specifically [this method](https://github.com/boto/boto3/blame/663bcaca2daa6d810bf9b12cbded436ba41102b1/boto3/compat.py#L87), being added. 
From what I've managed to uncover, [thanks to this thread in SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49712542/python-open-vs-gzip-open-and-file-mode), Pythons fileobjects aren't required to have their modes as str. The gzip module uses an int. Yes, they should be standardized inside their own stdlib, but gzip has been doing this for 20 years, so boto should probably adapt instead of the opposite.

### Regression Issue

- [ ] Select this option if this issue appears to be a regression.

### Expected Behavior

download_fileobject should work with any fileobject from the standard library.

### Current Behavior

download_fileobject fails when fileobjects' mode attribute is an int instead of a string.

### Reproduction Steps

`with gzip.open(path, 'file.gz', mode='wb+'): as gzip_file:`
`                   s3_client.download_fileobj(bucket, key, gzip_file,`
`                                           Config=TransferConfig(use_threads=False))`

### Possible Solution

treat ints as well as strings in the [is_append_mode](https://github.com/boto/boto3/blame/663bcaca2daa6d810bf9b12cbded436ba41102b1/boto3/compat.py#L87) method

### Additional Information/Context

_No response_

### SDK version used

1.38.9

### Environment details (OS name and version, etc.)

tested on windows 11 and ubuntu 24.10

issue_snapshot.title: getent returns misleading error when service override fails due to platform limitations on Alpine
issue_snapshot.body:
### Summary

When using the ansible.builtin.getent module with the service parameter and no key, the module returns an incorrect error message if the getent command fails due to unsupported service overrides (e.g., on Alpine Linux with musl libc).

The error message incorrectly states that a key could not be found—even when no key was provided. This leads to confusion and can make debugging harder, especially on multi-platform playbooks.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

getent

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version
ansible [core 2.18.7]
  config file = None
  configured module search path = ['/root/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3.12/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /root/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.12.11 (main, Jun  9 2025, 08:58:46) [GCC 13.2.1 20240309] (/usr/bin/python3)
  jinja version = 3.1.6
  libyaml = True
```

### Configuration

```console
# if using a version older than ansible-core 2.12 you should omit the '-t all'
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all
```

### OS / Environment

Alpine 3.20.6
Alpine 3.21.3

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```yaml (paste below)
  - name: Run getent with service override and no key
    ansible.builtin.getent:
      database: passwd
      service: files
    register: result
  
```


### Expected Results

The module should return an error message related to the actual cause of failure, such as:

`getent failed with rc=2. The specified service may be unsupported on this platform.`

This could be significantly clearer than blaming a missing key that was never supplied.

### Actual Results
On Alpine we get:

```console
TASK [Run getent with service override and no key] *************************************************************************************************************************************************************
fatal: [localhost]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "One or more supplied key could not be found in the database."}
```


In contrast in other OSes like Rocky we get:


```console
TASK [Run getent with service override and no key] *************************************************************************************************************************************************************
ok: [localhost]
```

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct

issue_snapshot.title: Alias not available during field transformation
issue_snapshot.body:
Hi, I'm not sure if this is a bug or a "feature" that is documented somewhere. At least, I haven't encountered it before, so I thought I'd better double-check.

Is it expected that the `alias` property is `None` during field transformation? Has this something to do with the fact that the class is not yet fully built at this stage? But since all information is pretty much already available at this point, I'm wondering if this is unintended ... 🤔 

```python
from attrs import define, field, fields


def f(cls, x):
    print("During field transformation:\n-------------------------------")
    for y in x:
        print(y.alias)
    return x


@define(field_transformer=f)
class C:
    _auto_stripped: int = field(default=0)
    _auto_stripped_with_alias: int = field(default=0, alias="_auto_stripped_with_alias")
    regular: int = field(default=0)
    regular_with_alias: int = field(default=0, alias="regular_with_alias")


print("\nAfter class creation:\n-------------------------------")
for fld in fields(C):
    print(fld.alias)
```

Gives:
```bash
During field transformation:
-------------------------------
None
_auto_stripped_with_alias
None
regular_with_alias

After class creation:
-------------------------------
auto_stripped
_auto_stripped_with_alias
regular
regular_with_alias
```

issue_snapshot.title: Botocore mistakenly expects a reason phrase in "100 Continue" responses
issue_snapshot.body:
### Describe the bug

When making HTTP requests, botocore sends a 100-continue request to the server, expecting a `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` response.

### Regression Issue

- [ ] Select this option if this issue appears to be a regression.

### Expected Behavior

The reason phrase is optional, so a `HTTP/1.1 100` response from the server is the correct behaviour.
Botocore should accept a `HTTP/1.1 100` response as correct.

### Current Behavior

If Botocore receives a `HTTP/1.1 100`, it interprets the response as not correct, and does not continue with the original request.

### Reproduction Steps

Start a service (locally) that sends `HTTP/1.1 100` responses to 100-continue requests, e.g. S3Mock:

```
docker run -e initialBuckets=my-bucket --rm -it -p 9090:9090 adobe/s3mock:4.0.0
```

Execute a `PutObject` request with a random file, e.g. the `README.rst` from the root of this repository, e.g. through `aws-cli` which uses boto3/botocore internally:

```
aws s3api put-object \
    --bucket x \
    --key y.txt \
    --content-type text/plain \
    --endpoint http://localhost:9090 \
    --body README.rst \
    --debug
```

The request will fail, as the Tomcat server used in S3Mock sends a `HTTP/1.1 100` as a response to the 100-continue request from botocore.

Example output:
```
2025-04-10 01:41:22,320 - MainThread - botocore.hooks - DEBUG - Event request-created.s3.PutObject: calling handler <bound method UserAgentString.rebuild_and_replace_user_agent_handler of <botocore.useragent.UserAgentString object at 0x1052779b0>>
```

```
    def _is_100_continue_status(self, maybe_status_line):
        parts = maybe_status_line.split(None, 2)

        # Check for HTTP/<version> 100 (Continue)\r\n
        return (
            len(parts) >= 2
            and parts[0].startswith(b'HTTP/')
            and parts[1] == b'100'
        )
```

issue_snapshot.title: Stubber attempting SSO Token retrieval
issue_snapshot.body:
### Describe the bug

When using a `Stubber` on a DynamoDB `Client`, the `Client` is still attempting to retrieve an AWS SSO Token, which it should not be doing. This issue may be occurring for other clients.

After digging, the error seems to be occurring when botocore is evaluating the ruleset for a dynamodb client. The ruleset contains a reference to the builtIn `"AWS::Auth::AccountId"` (which is not present in the S3 ruleset).

I believe this may be a regression issue. This is the first time I am encountering this issue and I have stubber the dynamo client previously.

versions:
`boto3 == 1.39.13`
`botocore == 1.39.13`
`python == 3.13.0`


### Regression Issue

- [x] Select this option if this issue appears to be a regression.

### Expected Behavior

Stubber should work for DynamoDB and no attempt at retrieving the AWS SSO Token should be made

### Current Behavior


When not logged into AWS through SSO, the following works using an S3 client:
```
s3_client = client("s3")
s3_stubber = Stubber(s3_client)

s3_stubber.add_response("get_object", {"Body": b"{}"})
s3_stubber.activate()

s3_response = s3_client.get_object(
    Bucket="TheBucket",
    Key="TheKey",
)

print(s3_response)
```

However, for a DynamoDB client:
```
db_client = client("dynamodb", region_name="us-east-1")
db_stubber = Stubber(db_client)

db_stubber.add_response("get_item", {})
db_stubber.activate()

db_response = db_client.get_item(
    TableName="TheTable",
    Key={},
)
print(db_response)
```

Causes an `SSOTokenLoadError` exception to be thrown. If `aws sso login` has been run before this, the exception is not raised (because the token can be located). However, if we are stubbing the client, we shouldn't need to be logged into AWS.


### Reproduction Steps

Run the previous code while the SSO is not logged in (may have to run `aws sso logout` explicitly.

### Possible Solution

_No response_

### Additional Information/Context

Running the following prevents the issue from happening, but it may cause other issues elsewhere while using the client
```
del db_client._ruleset_resolver._param_definitions["AccountId"]
```

### SDK version used

1.39.13

### Environment details (OS name and version, etc.)

Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.22631.5624], Python version 3.13.0
